notes: Single source of truth for native skills. Swift (HandsKit) implements an executor per name; Python reads it for routing prompts, shortlisting and training data. arg types: int, float, bool, string, enum, datetime, duration, path, app, url, contact. risk: safe (run immediately) | confirm (always ask first) | confirm_if_unsaved (ask only if the app reports unsaved changes). Free-text args (datetime, duration) are parsed by code, not by the model. Hidden args are filled by the brain from the request and left out of the router/ARGS/planner prompt text. executor: hands (default; HandsKit implements it) | brain (a Python tool in ml/src/brain/tools/ that computes deterministically and drives the Mac through HandsKit RPCs). New skills are appended at the end so existing choice ids stay stable.

special_options.name: MULTI_STEP
special_options.description: The request needs several UI steps or apps; hand off to the planner.

special_options.name: ASK
special_options.description: The request is ambiguous or missing required information; ask one short clarifying question.

special_options.name: REFUSE
special_options.description: The request is unsafe, or impossible on this Mac offline.

special_options.name: ANSWER
special_options.description: The user asked a question that needs a spoken answer, not an action.
